answer: Cap how much any single grader can earn from one author. Each grader's pay for scoring a given account falls off steeply after its first few grades of that account, and the cap resets only slowly. A sybil ring that routes its members to grade each other hits the cap almost at once, so mutual boosting stops paying, while honest graders who see many different authors keep full pay. The rule acts as a prism that splits a ring's traffic into a few thin beams, a lantern on who grades whom, and an inlet too narrow for a farm to push value through in bulk.
